newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: ANZ Bank staff vote to end NZ industrial action.
newsitem.headline: ANZ Bank staff vote to end NZ industrial action.

text.p: The Financial Sector Union on Thursday said New Zealand ANZ staff had narrowly voted to accept an improved offer from the bank and end a campaign of industrial action.

Union general secretary Paul Goulter said the bank had offered a 1.75 percent lump sum payment on top of the 3.5 percent salary increase. The bank had also agreed to involve the union in any negotiations to vary the collective contract.

"While ANZ staff were reluctant to accept the new proposal, there was general agreement that it goes a long way to addressing the issue of the bank's use of variations to undermine the collective contract and it also ensures that the collective contract will be offered to new staff," Goulter said.
"The salary offer has been accepted with full view of the need to ensure that the proposed introduction of a new salary system next year meets our members' requirements."
Auckland and Whangarei staff, who rejected the proposal, had taken strike action following the meeting. Auckland staff would meet again on Monday.
"These members were very angry with the ANZ's offer and have asked their negotiators to convey their feelings to the bank and seek an improved offer," Goulter said.
